Database.// TablePrefix: Prepended to the framework's own 12 tables (the 11 FrameworkEntityTypes.All entities plus schema_versions): users -> struo_users. Lower-case letters, digits and underscores, first character a letter, at most 16 characters; empty string = no prefix. Sample and fork tables are never prefixed. Changing it against a database that already holds framework tables makes the migrate command build a fresh, empty set under the new names; rename the existing tables to match first. Override via env Database__TablePrefix.
Database.// MigrationLockTimeoutSeconds: Seconds the migrate command waits for the migration lock before failing. Range 1-3600. Override via env Database__MigrationLockTimeoutSeconds.
Database.// MigrateOnStartup: true = apply pending migrations when the host starts, under the migration lock. false (the default) = the host refuses to start until the migrate command has run. Override via env Database__MigrateOnStartup.

Testing.// PostgresConnection: Opt-in PostgreSQL live tests: the migration tests, LiveRepositoryTests, PostgresOnlyTests, TestDatabaseLiveTests, and the API hosts and unit tests when STRUO_TEST_BACKEND selects this backend. Set in appsettings.Development.json to a DISPOSABLE database whose name contains 'test'; it must already exist, and the login needs create/drop-database rights (the migration tests write into it directly; the other live suites create their own databases next to it). An empty value makes the live tests return early as a pass, so judge them by per-test duration; with STRUO_TEST_BACKEND set to this backend the run fails instead. Env var STRUO_TEST_PG_CONNECTION overrides.

Struo.// ContentAssemblies: Assemblies scanned for [CmsCollection] content types. Add your content project's assembly name here (usually your content project's name), e.g. [ "Acme.Content" ]. The assembly must actually be resolvable via Assembly.Load, which means it must be registered in Struo.Api.deps.json (in practice, referenced by the host, e.g. via a ProjectReference) - a DLL merely sitting next to Struo.Api.dll is not enough - or the entry fails startup rather than being skipped.

Files.// DefaultStatus: Status given to a new upload: "published" (anyone with the file id can read it) or "draft" (only callers with file write access). Editors can switch a file afterwards. Any other value stops startup.

ImageTransform.// SizeSteps: Output sizes a requested width or height snaps UP to (above the last step, the last step applies, capped by MaxWidth/MaxHeight). Fewer steps = fewer cached variants. With fit=cover only the width snaps; the height follows the requested aspect ratio. Override via env Struo__Files__ImageTransform__SizeSteps__0, __1, ...
ImageTransform.// TransformableContentTypes: Source content types that are resized or converted. Any other image type (for example image/svg+xml) is served as the original bytes.
ImageTransform.// MaxConcurrentTransforms: Image transforms allowed to run at the same time across all requests. At least 2; anonymous requests may hold at most one slot fewer. Override via env Struo__Files__ImageTransform__MaxConcurrentTransforms.
ImageTransform.// QueueTimeoutSeconds: Seconds a request waits for a free transform slot before it gets 503 with code IMAGE_TRANSFORM_BUSY. 0 = do not wait.
ImageTransform.// CacheMaxBytes: Size cap of the on-disk variant cache in bytes (default 2 GB). Above it the least recently used variants are deleted. 0 = no cap.
ImageTransform.// MaxSourcePixels: Largest source (width x height) that is decoded. A larger source is served as the original bytes.

Localization.// Languages: Seeded by the core seed migration, which runs once; afterwards the table is the source of truth and languages are edited in the admin UI (System > Language). Codes must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,35} and be unique; DefaultLanguage must be one of them. Environment variables and appsettings.{Environment}.json merge this array by index: they can change an entry or append one (Localization__Languages__2__Code=ja plus __Name), but cannot remove one; to drop a language, edit this file.

Auth.// BootstrapAdmin: Seeded by the core seed migration, which runs once. Ships no password: Password must be set (Auth__BootstrapAdmin__Password, or appsettings.Production.json) in every environment, or the seed refuses to run; clearing Email seeds no admin. A configured password must satisfy Auth:Password and may not be 'admin'. Change the default Email too.
Auth.// Password: Plaintext password rules enforced at every write path (create user, change password). MinLength is also published to the SPA via GET /api/config for inline validation and generator length. MaxLength is a sanity bound only — Argon2id cost is fixed by its own parameters, not by input length. Override via env e.g. Auth__Password__MinLength=12 (read at startup; changing it requires a restart).
Auth.// Cookie: RequireSecure decides whether the session cookie is always Secure. Empty (null) follows the environment: Always outside Development, SameAsRequest in Development. true forces Secure everywhere; false lets the cookie travel over plain HTTP, for a Staging-like host that has no TLS in front of it. Configuring any Struo:Cors origin forces Secure regardless. Override via env e.g. Auth__Cookie__RequireSecure=false (read when the cookie options are first built).

// OpenApi: Enabled decides whether GET /openapi/v1.json and the Scalar explorer at /scalar are mapped; they publish the whole API surface with no authentication. Empty (null) follows the environment: Development only. true maps them in any environment, false in none. Override via env e.g. OpenApi__Enabled=true (read at startup; changing it requires a restart).
// ForwardedHeaders: Opt-in trust of the X-Forwarded-For/-Proto/-Host headers sent by a reverse proxy, so the API sees the real client address, scheme and host (the per-IP login limiter's buckets, and the https redirect URI OIDC builds, depend on them). Enabled=false by default: the headers are ignored. When Enabled=true, only requests whose TCP source matches KnownProxies (IP addresses) or KnownNetworks (CIDR ranges such as 172.16.0.0/12) are trusted, and at least one entry is required; a malformed entry or an empty pair of lists stops the host at startup, naming the key. Applied ahead of authentication, session rotation and rate limiting. Env vars set list entries by index (ForwardedHeaders__KnownNetworks__0=172.16.0.0/12); read at startup, changing them requires a restart.

RateLimiting.// Login: App-layer, per-CLIENT-IP login rate limiter (POST /api/auth/login only). Enabled=false by default: admin-backend staff typically share one NAT egress IP, so per-IP partitioning collapses a whole office into one shared bucket, locking staff out of their own logins rather than stopping a distributed attacker — even with forwarded headers configured correctly. Set Enabled=true only for a single-instance, directly-reachable deployment with no edge/WAF in front of it whose users do not share an egress IP (a personal or single-tenant install, or a development host); if enabled behind a reverse proxy, set ForwardedHeaders:Enabled with an explicit KnownProxies/KnownNetworks allowlist (section above) so each client gets its own bucket. RateLimiting:LoginAccount below is the layer that stays on by default. Override via env e.g. RateLimiting__Login__Enabled=true (read at startup; changing it requires a restart).
RateLimiting.// LoginAccount: App-layer, per-ACCOUNT login throttle (POST /api/auth/login only), backed by IDistributedCache, or by Redis when Redis:ConnectionString is set, and applied ahead of password verification. Counts every attempt against the account being attempted (from the request body), regardless of source IP, BEFORE the password is verified, so parallel guesses cannot slip past the limit; a successful login resets the counter. With Redis:ConnectionString set the counter is a Redis atomic INCR shared by every instance and login fails (5xx) while Redis is unreachable; otherwise it lives in the in-process distributed cache under a per-account lock. A known email can be kept locked by an attacker spending the limit (SSO sign-in is unaffected). Enabled=true by default — unlike RateLimiting:Login above, a per-account counter cannot collapse a shared-egress office into one bucket, since every account gets its own. Override via env e.g. RateLimiting__LoginAccount__PermitLimit=20 (read at startup; changing it requires a restart).
RateLimiting.// LoginConcurrency: Process-wide cap on how many logins (POST /api/auth/login) verify a password at the same time, so a flood of parallel attempts cannot pin every core on Argon2id. PermitLimit logins run at once, up to QueueLimit more wait for a slot, and the rest get 429 with Retry-After. Each instance enforces its own cap. Enabled=true by default. Override via env e.g. RateLimiting__LoginConcurrency__PermitLimit=8 (read at startup; changing it requires a restart).
RateLimiting.// Password: App-layer change-password rate limiter (PUT /api/users/{id}/password only), partitioned by the authenticated user id rather than client IP. Enabled=true is secure-by-default; set false in multi-pod deployments where this in-memory per-pod limiter cannot enforce a global limit. The partition key is the ACTING user, not the target: a super-admin doing bulk resets spends down their own single bucket and gets throttled past PermitLimit, while every target's own budget is untouched — this also means the endpoint can never be used to lock a victim out of changing their own password. Raise PermitLimit here if the admin-side throttling becomes a problem. Override via env e.g. RateLimiting__Password__PermitLimit=20 (read at startup; changing it requires a restart).

// Oidc: External sign-in through OpenID Connect providers, one entry per provider under Providers:<id> (id: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Each enabled provider adds a sign-in button and needs DisplayName, Authority, ClientId and ClientSecret. Icon is a token the admin UI maps to a glyph; Order sorts the buttons ascending (ties by id). CallbackPath is the path the provider redirects back to; the shipped entries set it explicitly and an entry without it uses /signin-oidc-<id>. Each provider needs its own path. Register that path, relative to the site origin, as the redirect URI at the provider. Prompt is sent as the prompt parameter of the authorize request: select_account (default) always shows the account picker, login forces re-entering credentials, consent re-asks for consent, none never shows any page; values may be combined with a space (e.g. login consent); empty sends no prompt. Any other value fails startup for an enabled provider. A multi-tenant Entra Authority (common, organizations, consumers) needs AllowedTenantId or AllowedEmailDomains; a Google Authority needs AllowedEmailDomains. ClientSecret is deliberately absent from this file and must never be committed: set it with env Oidc__Providers__<id>__ClientSecret, with user-secrets (dotnet user-secrets set "Oidc:Providers:<id>:ClientSecret" <value> --project src/Struo.Api), or in a gitignored appsettings.Development.json. Override any key via env Oidc__Providers__<id>__<Key>. ReturnUrlDefault applies to every provider.
